## Iteration cand_0001 — encode compensation policy in code + add atomic-modify and reservation-loop tools

- `send_certificate` (cluster: unauthorized compensation, task 37-t1): in-body guard — `amount` must be a positive multiple of 50 ($100×pax / $50×pax); else raise an actionable ValueError pointing to transfer_to_human_agents.

- ADD `modify_reservation` (cluster: multi-step write stall, tasks 17-t0/23-t0): one atomic WRITE that applies cabin/flights + baggages + passengers by delegating to the existing update primitives. Primitives kept (all load-bearing for passing/flaky tasks, so none removable).
- ADD `get_reservations(reservation_ids)` (cluster: stops enumerating reservations, tasks 8-t1/17-t1): loop READ tool returning all requested reservations in one call with per-id error entries.

- send_certificate guard fixes 37-t1's $116 voucher pollution → DB stays clean == gold. SAFE: no passing/flaky task calls send_certificate with a valid amount; fires only on non-multiple-of-50 → bounded.

- modify_reservation lets the agent complete 17's 3 changes / 23's rebuild in ONE call instead of stalling. SAFE: pure add; delegates to same primitive bodies; verified baggages-only composite == primitive (task-12 identical DB), cabin-only refund == primitive (−5244).
- get_reservations removes the "stopped after 4/5" / "checked only 1st" failure mode. SAFE: read-only add.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — iteration 1 (seed only).

- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: (a) task 11 refund-number COMMUNICATE check ($5244) — DB matches, only spoken value wrong; no safe code lever (return-shape risk per field-notes). (b) tasks 19/40 single-write no-op in one trial — looks like truncated sim turns. (c) task 23's cancel + 3 per-passenger rebook needs the agent to actually issue the bookings; modify_reservation doesn't cover the cancel+book split — a `rebook_per_passenger` composite is the next design to try if 23 stays 0.

- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is REJECTED, the likeliest culprit is modify_reservation/get_reservations being additive-only (weak agent may not select them — field-notes §2 warns composites often land at/below parent); in that case next iteration drop the additive tools and lean purely on more in-body guards.

- Focus next iteration: if accepted, target task 8 wrong-flight (needs the agent to ground on the past reservation) and the task-11 refund arithmetic; if rejected, keep only the send_certificate guard and add more bounded in-body guards.

- Strategy tried: parallel read-only diagnosis subagents (one per trajectory group) → cluster → one bounded in-body guard (send_certificate) + two additive delegating tools (modify_reservation, get_reservations). Result pending gate.

- Key structural constraint discovered: EVERY write primitive is used by a passing or flaky task (12→baggages, 40→passengers, 11/37→flights, 25→book, 19/37→cancel). So the standard "add composite + REMOVE primitive to make it un-skippable" pattern is BLOCKED here — composites can only be additive/opt-in, which weakens their effect on a mid-tier reader.
